svg.title: Three examples of LLM judge critiques
svg.desc: Critiques identify answer leakage, memorized textbook bugs, and a source cited without being retrieved. Full selectable text appears beneath the figure in the blog post.
svg.text: The benchmark had leaked its own answers, and the difficulty it reported was an artifact of that.

text.tspan: “Task assets leak oracle verdicts inside supposedly neutral evidence files that instruction.md says
should be tables/figures. Task-001 supplementary.md line 12 ‘Note: This table does NOT include MViT-B
or Uniformer-B as requested.’ [...] These directly disclose deflection/partial gaps, trivializing
intended charitability-bias detection. Consequently baselines achieve ceiling [...] contradicting
benchmark_spec.md hypothesis that baselines will achieve < 0.6 [...] Perfect Oracle and baseline
scores indicate shallow short-horizon tasks where leaked notes replace multi-hop reasoning over hidden
logs. [...] Scaling to real OpenReview threads without leaked notes would be fundamentally different
difficulty, so current design does not support principled scaling.”

svg.text: The tasks were textbook bugs the solvers had already memorized.

text.tspan: “Two tasks (task-001 missing zero_grad, task-002 drop_last zero-batch) are classic well-known pitfalls
with StackOverflow documentation, likely memorized, contributing to near-ceiling baselines (Glimmer

svg.text: A source was cited but never retrieved.

text.tspan: “Source-004 claims ‘Causal Inference Book Chapter 6 - Confounding’ with origin
sources/causal_book_epi_ch6.html is byte-identical (SHA256 c5ba7e61..., size 289002) to homepage HTML
titled ‘Home | Chan School of Public Health’, lacking any Chapter 6 confounding tabular content. [...]
Replace or remove manifest record source-004 [...] and every dependent claim or grading anchor.”
